states: Private mock-mode stack (backend :7867, Vite :5387) built from this branch with a dev-only -overlay tagging the ci-runner-01 and analytics-batch-01 demo profiles pulse-relaxed (68 relaxed Proxmox VMs); default guest thresholds CPU 80/75, memory 85/80, disk 90/85

Before the change on the same stack: relaxed ci-runner-117 at 88% memory drew a red (critical) memory bar while the engine raises no alert below 92%, and its Alerts thresholds row showed 80/85/90 with nothing naming the tag

Proxmox guests filtered by tags:pulse-relaxed: all 66 running relaxed rows coloured by the relaxed band (warning from 80%, critical from 92% memory); analytics-batch-70 at 87% memory reads warning (yellow) at 800px and at 375px
Control: untagged Proxmox guests in the same band stay critical (red): redis-cache-259 92%, redis-cache-379 91%, checkout-web-02 92%, postgres-primary-293 86%, at desktop and 375px

Alerts > Thresholds > Proxmox > VMs & Containers, analytics-batch-70: card layout (default page width, every viewport up to 2560px) and table layout (full-width mode at 2560px) both show "Proxmox tag pulse-relaxed: alerts at CPU 95% · Memory 92% · Disk 95%" under the name, with the explanatory title; the metric cells keep the configured 80% / 85% / 90%
At 375px the line sits at full card width under the card header in two lines; pulse-relaxed and each threshold stay unbroken (whitespace-nowrap spans); no horizontal page scroll (scrollWidth 375)
Untagged guest postgres-primary-293 on the thresholds page shows no relaxed line
No console errors from the final build; one transient ReferenceError came from an intermediate HMR state between two edits and did not recur after reload

After this pass the only change to these files was prettier wrapping the JSX attributes of AlertResourceRelaxedTriggers.tsx onto separate lines (no output change), plus a rebase onto main that touched none of the changed paths

After a review, relaxGuestThresholdValue now fills a legacy bare trigger number with the backend's fixed five-point clear instead of the configured hysteresis margin, matching ensureHysteresisThreshold. The current backend sends hysteresis objects, so this branch is not reachable from the stack exercised above; the rendered bars and lines checked here resolve through the unchanged object path, and the numeric branch is pinned by metricThresholds.test.ts at margins 5 and 10
